result.title: EEG2MCU: Sensing-to-Execution Co-Design for Wearable EEG Inference
result.comment: 7 pages, 9 figures, 3 tables. Accepted at DATE 2027
result.summary: Wearable EEG inference is constrained not only by model size, but also by the channel-dependent sensing front end that must process high-dimensional inputs before compact downstream computation. We present EEG2MCU, a sensing-to-execution co-design framework that treats electrode count as a hardware design variable through task-aware montage selection. EEG2MCU retains a compact time-frequency representation and generates only the INT8 regions required by each first-layer tile, avoiding full input materialization. Halo reuse and access-aware placement across Flash, SRAM, and tightly coupled memory further reduce redundant generation and data movement. On a Cortex-M7 MCU, EEG2MCU reduces peak SRAM by 11.38x relative to the baseline, including a 1.71x reduction from the 62-to-19 electrode montage, while reducing latency by 2.57x and energy by 2.48x. It retains 94-96% of full-montage accuracy, demonstrating practical high-dimensional EEG inference under tight embedded-resource constraints.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 EEG2MCU 的「感知到执行」协同设计框架，将电极数量视为可设计的硬件变量，通过任务感知的 montage 选择、只按需生成首层所需的 INT8 时频区域并做多级存储复用，在 Cortex-M7 上大幅降低 SRAM、延迟与能耗，同时保留大部分全 montage 精度。
AI.relevance_reason: 其按任务挑选输入通道、只惰性生成被使用区域的思路，可能为 LVR 中在算力与带宽约束下筛选视觉证据、按需计算特征提供借鉴，可供核查其选通道准则能否迁移到 token/区域级选择与动态计算。
